review.mode: Independent read-only design and implementation review; no real network or file writes
designFindings: One journal is participating-caller scope, not credential-wide or distributed coordination.
Unknown outcomes must block the same object and reopening; they do not preserve unseen remote headers.
Admission must precede a fresh notice claim to avoid stranding unsent notices on cooldown rejection.
Measure spacing after response completion, with monotonic enforcement in-process.
Only ownership of an exclusive reservation authorizes a request, not equal existing content.
Production GET verification appends rate records and must not be described as filesystem-read-only.
implementationDefectsFixed: False/zero request overrides and explicitly passing the production worker could bypass the required budget.
Reservation and notice-claim persistence could consume the remaining admission deadline before HTTP dispatch.
Retry-After HTTP-date parsing accepted trailing garbage.
review.finalReview: No remaining findings in the three narrowly reviewed fixes. In-memory probes confirmed: Invalid transports and unguarded explicit production transport are rejected. Canonical dates pass; trailing garbage is rejected. Delays during reservation or notice-claim persistence prevent transport dispatch and retain unresolved reservations. All three prior findings are resolved. No files written or network called; full suite not rerun.
review.testWorkerScope: Wrote only tests/test_source_metadata_request_budget.py; 28 cases reported passing independently. Parent final frozen-source run is authoritative.
limits: No actual scheduler, live GitHub comment, provider account or hosted persistence tested.
Trusted stable local journal ancestors, no rollback/deletion defense or power-loss guarantee.
Final follow-up review was narrow to the three reported fixes, not a claim to exhaustive absence of bugs.

findings: Production GitHub delivery now requires retained request admission and cooldown state.
Admission precedes a fresh notice claim, so cooldowns no longer strand unsent notices.
A successful last-slot POST retains its returned ID while verification waits.
Unknown requests remain blocking evidence; activation, durable hosting, operator recovery, real reporting, physical-device and exact-release gates remain open.
disagreements: GET-only verification now writes separate rate records; it does not mutate notice/source evidence.
One local journal and shared batch object do not provide credential-wide coordination, rollback protection or a running service.
